terms.gloss: a spring: a coil or strip of metal that gives way and returns
terms.comment: Antiquity had no word for it. Morgan–Owens gives elastrum from Kant (1755); it is not in Lewis & Short. The word is made from the Greek ἐλαστός, and its vowels are short. The shape of a coiled spring is a spīra, a coil.

terms.gloss: spring, springiness: the tendency of a thing to return to its shape
terms.comment: Greek ἐλατήρ, “driver”, with its long ē; Morgan–Owens gives it from Pecquet (seventeenth century) for the springiness of the air, and it is also said of the device.

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.vv. spring (device); spring, elasticity.
